---
title: "An else at the start of a line is a syntax error"
ref: FLW-07
categories: [Control flow]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "`\"negative\"`, as in any other language"
versions: "All"
source: "safer-r, The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
#| eval: false
x <- -5
if (x > 0) {
  "positive"
}
else {
  "negative"
}
```
:::

Run this block: R prints "Error: unexpected 'else' in "else"", then evaluates `"negative"` as a standalone statement and prints it, then complains about the final `}` with "unexpected '}'". The right result does appear, buried between two errors.

## Why

At the console, and in a script run line by line, R evaluates a statement as soon as it is complete. After the `}` on the fourth line, `if (x > 0) { "positive" }` is a complete statement, with no `else`. The next line starts with `else`, which cannot start a statement: syntax error.

The same code runs fine inside a function or any other block between braces, because R only ends the statement at the block's closing brace. Code copied from a function to the console therefore breaks for no apparent reason.

## The fix

Always write `} else {` on the same line.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
x <- -5
if (x > 0) {
  "positive"
} else {
  "negative"
}
```
:::
